finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice by ID with no authentication or ownership check (IDOR / broken access control). The sibling route /my/invoice/<inv_id> enforces inv['customer'] == g.user['id'], so the omission looks like an oversight.
finding.source: The inv_id URL path parameter, supplied by any unauthenticated or authenticated remote requester.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) at line 10, which returns the full invoice record, including the customer field and any other invoice data.

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> is registered with no auth decorator.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) fetches the record by the caller-supplied ID with no check on who is asking.
The record is returned to the caller as JSON.
For comparison, the /my/ route checks ownership against g.user['id'] and returns 404 on mismatch. This check is missing from the route above.

finding.guards_checked: No before_request handler, auth decorator or g.user check applies to this route. invoices.py is the only file in the repository, so no external middleware is visible. Only the /my/ routes compare the customer to g.user. If invoice IDs are guessable or sequential, enumeration is trivial.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no decorator, before_request hook or g.user check, and returns jsonify(inv) for any ID, while the sibling route at invoices.py:16 enforces ownership; invoices.py is the only file in the repo, so no external middleware is visible.
